Persist browser data only when the user value and threat model justify it.

Persistence can make an application feel dependable, but it also gives data a longer life than the current page. This chapter shows how to keep a useful local workspace across refreshes while protecting the value at the persistence boundary and making the security trade-offs explicit.

Why this boundary matters

The FeatureCell continues to work with plain in-memory State while encryption protects the finalized value before persistence writes it to browser storage. Encrypting before persisting keeps storage concerns out of application code, but it is not a complete browser-security strategy: key management, XSS exposure, storage lifetime, and the sensitivity of the data still require deliberate decisions.

Use this structure for

  • restoring non-sensitive preferences across page refreshes
  • keeping a local workspace or draft available during a session
  • retaining browser data when its value justifies its storage lifetime

By the end of this chapter

You will have encryption and Session Storage persistence registered in the correct pipeline boundary, a plain in-memory Feature State, and a clear understanding of what this protection covers—and what your application security design must still address.

Step 34: Configure Encrypt and Persist Behaviors
↑ top

This step adds encryption and persistence to the same character collection. The AES-256 Encrypt behavior protects the finalized pipeline value before the Session Storage Persist behavior writes it to browser storage. The FeatureCell continues to work with plain in-memory State.

Register withAes256EncryptBehavior and withSessionStoragePersistBehavior in app.config.ts, with Encrypt registered before Persist.

Take Action
  1. Install the package.
  2. Open app.config.ts.
  3. Import withAes256EncryptBehavior and withSessionStoragePersistBehavior from .
  4. Add both behaviors to the behavior list passed to provideFeatureCell(). The order does not matter when adding behaviors. 
npm install @sdux-vault/addons

  devMode: true,
  bypassingLicensing: true

Step 35: Encrypt Feature State
↑ top

AES-256-GCM encryption protects the finalized Feature State before it reaches persistence. It runs after Resolve, Merge, Operators, Filters, and Reducers have completed, so the FeatureCell continues to expose the same plain in-memory value to the application.

The example uses a static salt for teaching purposes so you can repeat the tutorial and inspect the configuration. In a secure application, obtain salt material dynamically from an appropriate secure configuration source and keep it stable for data that must be decrypted later.

Take Action
  1. Open example.service.ts and locate the setAes256Secret() configuration.
  2. Review the static salt and identify where production code would load stable salt material dynamically.
  3. Use the Results panel to compare plain Feature State with the encrypted envelope.
What to Look For
  • Encryption does not change the value exposed by the FeatureCell.
  • AES-256-GCM provides confidentiality and integrity at the persistence boundary.
  • A stable salt is required to decrypt previously persisted ciphertext.

Step 36: Persist Feature State
↑ top

Add withSessionStoragePersistBehavior after encryption to store the encrypted envelope in browser sessionStorage. Refresh the page and the persisted state remains available in that same tab. Close the tab and the session storage is cleared, so it is not durable application storage.

The example intentionally provides initialState while allowing persisted State to take priority. During hydration the persisted value is used by design; the initial value is not loaded into the active FeatureCell and is overwritten with undefined when no persisted value is available. This makes the persistence boundary explicit instead of silently mixing two sources of truth.

Take Action
  1. Persisted state is handled through the pipeline. Once registered in the there is nothing more to configure.
  2. Make a character change and inspect the persisted output.
  3. Refresh the page in the same tab and verify that the collection is restored.
What to Look For
  • Persist observes the finalized value after encryption and does not participate in state computation.
  • Session storage is scoped to one tab and survives reloads only within that tab.
  • Persisted State takes priority over initialState by design.

Step 37: Complete Encrypt and Persist Tutorial
↑ top

You now have a complete persistence boundary: pipeline stages compute and validate plain Feature State, AES-256 encrypts the finalized value, and session storage preserves it for reloads in the current tab.

Take Action
  1. Refresh the page and confirm the session-scoped collection is restored.
  2. Close the tab, open the example again, and confirm that the tab-scoped value is gone.
Tutorial Summary
  • Encrypt and Persist behaviors run at the persistence boundary.
